Speed and size limits

Source: vignettes/speed.Rmd
speed.Rmd

How long do pedkindraw’s computations and drawings take, and how large a pedigree can each one handle? This page answers from two timing records made on one machine in November 2026, which timed pedkindraw’s own installed code beside the kinship2 and Pedixplorer functions that do the same. Each table says which record it comes from: its date, the pedkindraw commit timed, the versions of kinship2 and Pedixplorer and the machine. Every number on the page was checked against the records’ result files by a script, tools/checkSpeedTables.R in pedkindraw’s GitHub repository, which also holds the records (tools/timing/results/). The page runs no code.

The machine and the method

Each run was a fresh R process. It loaded the package being timed and those its call needs, built its input before the clock started, and timed one call. A step a user must run first was inside the timed call: pedkindraw’s kinship() time includes findGeneration(), and kinship2’s kinship by family includes makefamid(). For each function and size, smallest first, a warm-up run came first, which was also the test of whether that size fits; then three measured runs, and each figure on this page is their median. A run failed when it passed 120 seconds from the call’s start or 32 GB of memory (29.8 GiB, R’s limit on its heap or a watchdog on the process’s memory), and the sizes after a function’s first failure were not run. Each run started only once at least half of the CPU was idle, waiting at most 10 minutes; other work on the machine went on beside the runs, and the table below gives the share of the CPU idle as each run started.

pedkindraw was built from the commit each record names and installed as CRAN installs a package, and each run checked that it loaded that copy. kinship2 and Pedixplorer were the versions each record names, from CRAN and Bioconductor.

The pedigrees are synthetic colonies of 300 to 100,000 animals, made by one seeded generator that grows a colony a year at a time, and, for the drawings, the 375-animal example pedigree that comes with pedkindraw (system.file("extdata", "obfuscated_rhesus_mhc_ped.csv", package = "pedkindraw")). The functions that shrink a pedigree or find an unrelated set use a seeded 30% of the animals as genotyped and 10% as affected; those that start from probands use 5 seeded animals with a known sire.

The two records, on one machine: Apple M2 Max (Mac14,6), 12 cores, 96 GiB, R 4.6.2. Both timed the same pedkindraw R code, git tree ac123b7.

Computation

The tables give the seconds each function took, by the number of animals, with pedkindraw’s function first and then kinship2’s and Pedixplorer’s that do the same. A figure is the median of three measured runs, to three significant figures, and “<0.001” is under a millisecond. A failed size says how it failed: “time”, past 120 seconds; “memory”, past 32 GB; “error”, the function stopped with an error. The sizes after a failure were not run and are empty. kinship2 and Pedixplorer were given each input in their own coding.

The computations the packages share

What each computation is:

  • Kinship, autosomal: the kinship coefficient of every pair of animals, the chance that a gene drawn at random from each of the two is the same copy inherited from a common ancestor, as a matrix with a row and a column for each animal.
  • Kinship, autosomal, sparse or by family: the same values stored as a sparse matrix, which keeps only the pairs above 0; kinship2’s nearest is its kinship within each family, makekinship(), after makefamid(), and Pedixplorer has none.
  • Kinship, X chromosome: the kinship of genes on the X chromosome, which needs each animal’s sex.
  • Generation depth: each animal’s generation, 0 for a founder (both parents unknown) and otherwise one more than the later of its parents.
  • Family (connected component): a family number for each animal, shared by every animal linked to it through sires, dams and offspring.
  • Shrink to 16 bits: animals removed until the pedigree’s bit size (see “Bit size” below) is 16 or less, keeping the genotyped and affected animals that carry the most information; each step tries every animal that could go and removes the one that lowers the bit size most, so the time grows much faster than the pedigree.
  • Unrelated set: as many genotyped animals as can be found of which no two are related.
  • Probands and their ancestors: a chosen group of animals (the probands) and all of their ancestors, the rest dropped.
  • Probands and their descendants: the probands and all of their descendants.
  • Build a pedigree object: kinship2’s pedigree() and Pedixplorer’s Pedigree() turn a table of animals into the object their other functions take; pedkindraw works on the data frame itself and has no such step.

The other functions kinship2 or Pedixplorer also has

  • Bit size: kinship2’s measure of a pedigree’s size, twice the number of animals with a known parent less the number of founders.
  • Unavailable animals to trim: the animals shrinking removes first: those not genotyped with no genotyped descendant, and the founders their removal leaves of no use.
  • Available, uninformative animals to trim: the genotyped animals that add no information: no animal’s parent, not affected, and both parents known and genotyped.
  • One available affected animal to trim: one step of shrinking’s last trim, the genotyped animal of a chosen affected status, no animal’s parent, whose removal leaves the smallest bit size.
  • Family check: each animal’s family number compared with the family trees its parent links form, family by family.
  • IBD matrix from pairs: identity-by-descent values written one line per pair of animals, as programs such as SOLAR write them, made into a sparse matrix with a row and a column for each animal.
  • Near relatives (distance 3): the animals within a distance of 3 of the probands (a grandparent, half sibling, uncle or aunt is at 3) and the parents that join their families.
  • Remove 5 animals: 5 listed animals, each with a known sire and no offspring, removed from the pedigree.
  • A kinship2 object as a data frame: a kinship2 pedigree object turned back into a table of animals, pedkindraw’s by asPedFrame().
  • A Pedixplorer object as a data frame: the same for a Pedixplorer Pedigree object.
  • Add rows for missing parents: a row added for each sire or dam that has none of its own.
  • Count offspring: the number of offspring of each animal.
  • Recode a pedigree file’s values: other programs’ codes for an unknown parent and for sex rewritten into the package’s own.
  • Founder or not: for each animal, whether it is a founder.
  • Generation depth, mates aligned: the generation depth with, where it can be done, an offspring’s sire and dam in the same generation, as a drawing needs; the three packages align by rules of their own.

The functions only pedkindraw has

  • Check a pedigree: every problem found in a pedigree, one row per problem, such as an animal that is its own ancestor or a parent with no row.
  • Matings: each sire and dam with offspring together, once, with the number of offspring they share.
  • Correct parents’ sex: the sex of each animal listed as a sire made male and as a dam made female.
  • Add back second parents: the known parent an animal lost in trimming put back.
  • Remove uninformative founders: founders that appear only once removed, until none is left.
  • Remove added animals: the placeholder rows added for unknown parents removed.
  • Probands’ pedigree: the probands and all of their ancestors.
  • Parents of 5 animals: the sire and dam of each of 5 animals.
  • Offspring of 5 animals: the offspring of 5 animals.
  • Founders’ ids: the ids of the founders.
  • Has both parents: whether one animal has both parents known.
  • Animals with one parent: the ids of the animals with only one known parent.
  • Check twin pairs: a table of twin pairs checked against the pedigree: both ids in it, twins with the same sire and dam, identical twins of one sex.

What this means for pedkindraw’s users:

  • Its kinship is as fast as kinship2’s: a dense kinship matrix of 30,000 animals took 28.1 seconds, against kinship2’s 29.3, and no kinship finished 100,000 animals within the 32 GB allowed.
  • findPedigreeNumber() is the one function much slower than its counterparts at the largest size: 12.4 seconds at 100,000 animals, against 0.609 for kinship2’s and 0.644 for Pedixplorer’s.
  • shrinkPedigree() shrank 3,000 animals in 89.5 seconds; kinship2’s and Pedixplorer’s passed 120 seconds at 3,000 and 1,000 animals.
  • findUnrelated() finished 100,000 animals in 33.9 seconds; kinship2’s and Pedixplorer’s stopped after 10,000.
  • findAvailAffected() took 83.3 seconds at 100,000 animals, and findGeneration(alignMates = TRUE) 60.6 seconds at 10,000 and more than 120 at 30,000, as the other two packages’ alignments did.
  • pedkindraw takes a data frame, so it has no pedigree object to build; kinship2’s and Pedixplorer’s functions need theirs first.

“Process peak”: the process’s largest resident memory there. “R heap peak”: the most R’s heap held above its starting point, read at its garbage collections. macOS’s resident figure leaves out compressed memory, so near the limit the two can disagree, as for the sparse kinship at 30,000.

Drawing

Seconds from a pedigree to a drawing, on a canvas of 3,600 by 1,500 pixels for the web pages and pictures. The rows time different things:

  • web page: findGeneration(), makePedigreeMatingLayout() and drawPedigreeDiagram() in R, the page saved, then the page opened in Chrome until its first drawn frame: R’s and the browser’s time together. The lines are rectilinear, the default, or direct.
  • SVG, PDF and PNG file: savePedigreeDiagram() of a drawing built before the clock, so these rows time only what saving adds, on the function’s own page.
  • diagram data: makePedigreeDiagramData() alone, the nodes and edges of a simpler drawing, without the layout that takes most of a drawing’s time.
  • picture and plotly page: kinship2’s and Pedixplorer’s drawings, timed the same way as pedkindraw’s page; Pedixplorer’s plotly page is drawn by the call its own app makes. kinship2 and Pedixplorer were given a placeholder for the missing parent of an animal with one known parent, which they need; pedkindraw drew each pedigree as it is.

“time”: R and the browser together passed 120 seconds. “error”: the function stopped with an error; Pedixplorer’s alignment of parents stopped with an error on the first colony, of 300 animals, and its own warning suggests turning it off, so it was also timed with alignment off. “not timed”: the SVG and PNG files at 3,000 animals were not timed, because the drawing they save, built before the clock, took longer than the 300 seconds allowed for setup, so the save never started; the save itself did not fail. A save’s three runs can differ by one slow run, at most about twice as long as the other two in this record; the median holds against it.

Can a reader use a drawing that large? Judged by eye by the package’s author from the record’s pages, a pedkindraw drawing can be read up to 1,000 animals, zoomed in: an animal found by its id, by zooming or with “Select by id”, and its lines followed to its parents. A drawing of 1,000 animals took 16 seconds; with direct lines, 2,000 animals took 106. pedkindraw’s drawing code began as a copy of nprcgenekeepr’s. runPedigreeApp() asks before it draws more than 1,000 animals.

What these numbers cannot tell you

  • Another machine’s times: these are one Mac’s, with other work running beside the runs.
  • A smaller machine’s limits: the runs were allowed 32 GB of memory, and the kinship matrices of the largest sizes need most of that; on a machine with less memory they stop at a smaller size.
  • Another browser’s drawing time: the browser’s part was timed in Chrome.
  • A real pedigree’s times: these pedigrees are synthetic colonies, and the shape of a pedigree matters as much as its size: the drawing vignette’s times for pedigrees taken from nprcgenekeepr’s example pedigree differ from these at the same size.

Where next

vignette("pedkindraw", package = "pedkindraw") takes the 375-animal example pedigree from its records to a drawing, and vignette("drawing", package = "pedkindraw") shows what a drawing shows and how to change it. ?pedkindraw lists every function by what it does.
